definition_en: empty, swaggering boastfulness; a boaster's manner or talk
core_image: 一个插着羽毛帽的武士拍着胸脯高声吹嘘，话音越大盔甲越显得空
scene: 赛前发布会上他唾沫横飞。His braggadocio filled the room, promising victory before the first round.
sceneCN: 这里 braggadocio 是「大话、吹牛的姿态」（第 1 个义项：空洞的自夸言行）；句意是他的豪言壮语灌满全场，第一回合还没打就预支了胜利。

derivatives.zh: 词源基础动词，义为「吹嘘」
由同根加表人后缀构成，义为「自夸的人」
由同根加表人后缀构成，义为「吹牛者」

senses.title: Empty, swaggering boastfulness
senses.titleCN: 空洞的大话；虚张的夸口
senses.definition: talk that boasts loudly without backing deeds or facts
senses.definitionCN: 高声自夸却没有行动或事实支撑的言谈
senses.why: The word was coined for a character who is all mouth, so the name names the mouthiness itself.
senses.whyCN: 该词本是为一个「只有嘴上功夫」的角色而造，于是名字转指这种空嘴作风。

senses.title: A boaster's manner
senses.definition: a swaggering, self-important style of behaving and speaking
senses.definitionCN: 张扬自大、自我抬举的言谈举止风格
senses.example: Behind the braggadocio he was shy.
senses.exampleCN: 吹牛的姿态背后，他其实很腼腆。
senses.why: What the character does becomes a style anyone can put on, a mask available to all.
senses.whyCN: 角色的一举一动泛化为一种可供任何人佩戴的风格面具。

senses.title: A person given to boasting
senses.definition: a boaster; a person of empty talk
senses.definitionCN: 惯于自夸的人；满嘴空话者
senses.example: Every company has one braggadocio at the bar.
senses.exampleCN: 每家酒馆里都有一个 braggadocio 式的人物。
senses.why: The original character name applied first to the person, then to his talk.
senses.whyCN: 原本的角色名先指人，后才转指其言谈。

senses.title: Puffed style in writing or speech
senses.definition: inflated, high-flown style in prose or rhetoric
senses.definitionCN: 行文或修辞中浮夸虚胀的风格
senses.example: The general's memoirs sink into braggadocio.
senses.exampleCN: 那位将军的回忆录堕入了浮夸之风。
senses.why: Spoken swagger transfers to the written voice, since prose can strut like a person.
senses.whyCN: 口头的张扬转移到笔头，因为文章也能像人一样昂首阔步。

senses.title: Pretended strength or courage
senses.definition: an outward show of confidence hiding fear or weakness
senses.definitionCN: 以外表的自信掩盖恐惧或软弱
senses.example: His braggadocio hid a fear of failing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的大话掩盖着对失败的恐惧。
senses.why: A mask implies a face beneath; the word always hints at the hollow inside.
senses.whyCN: 面具意味着面具下还有脸；这个词总暗示内里的空洞。

senses.title: Cultural swagger of a group
senses.definition: a shared style of bold self-assertion, as in music or sport
senses.definitionCN: 音乐、体育等圈子里集体性的张扬自许风格
senses.example: The track's braggadocio defined the whole genre.
senses.exampleCN: 这首曲子的张扬气质定义了整个流派。
senses.why: Individual manner becomes group identity when many adopt the same mask.
senses.whyCN: 当众人戴上同一种面具，个人姿态便升格为群体认同。

senses.title: Boastful challenge before a contest
senses.definition: loud pre-match or pre-fight talk aimed at opponents
senses.definitionCN: 针对对手的赛前高声叫阵之词
senses.exampleCN: 赛前的叫阵大话正是卖票的噱头。
senses.why: Since the character bragged before fighting, the word fits the moment before contests.
senses.whyCN: 既然原型角色总在打斗前夸口，此词便贴合赛事开打前的时刻。

senses.title: The literary character himself
senses.definition: the boasting character Braggadocchio in Spenser's poem, the word's source
senses.definitionCN: 斯宾塞诗中的自夸者布拉加多丘，本词的出处
senses.example: Spenser's Braggadocchio rides without ever fighting.
senses.exampleCN: 斯宾塞笔下的布拉加多丘骑着马却从不接战。
senses.why: Remembering the character keeps the word honest: it has always meant the hollow knight.
senses.whyCN: 记住原型角色，词义便不会走样：它从来都指那个空心的骑士。

intro.en: Braggadocio was coined by Edmund Spenser in The Faerie Queene (1590) as the name of a boastful knight, built on brag with a mock-Italian ending.
intro.cn: braggadocio 由斯宾塞在《仙后》（1590）中创造，是一名自夸骑士之名，以 brag 为基、缀以仿意大利语词尾。

items.en: The base is brag, Middle English for loud talk and boasting.
items.cn: 词基是 brag，中古英语中指大声说话与吹嘘。

items.en: Spenser modeled the name on Italian braggadocchio, cheekily adding -occhio as if for an Italian bravo.
items.cn: 斯宾塞仿意大利语 braggadocchio 造名，戏谑地加上 -occhio 词尾，像给意大利剑客起名。

items.en: In The Faerie Queene, Braggadocchio claims knightly fame but never fights, the perfect empty boaster.
items.cn: 在《仙后》中，布拉加多丘自诩骑士声名却从不作战，是完美的空心吹牛者。

items.en: The name became a common noun for any empty boaster, lowercase and general.
items.cn: 十七世纪该名转为普通名词，小写作泛指一切空谈的吹牛者。

items.en: Use shifted mainly to the talk and manner rather than the person.
items.cn: 用法重心渐由人转为其言谈与做派。

items.en: Modern English keeps the swaggering manner sense, popular in sport and music criticism.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「张扬做派」义，常见于体育与音乐评论。

note.en: The word is a one-off coinage; its look-alikes are all in the brag family, its sound-alikes merely end alike.
note.cn: 该词是一次性造词；形近词都在 brag 词族内，音近词只是词尾相仿。

entries.definitionCN: 惯于自夸者；同根表人名词
薄伽丘之姓；词尾相仿纯属斯宾塞的戏仿

entries.definition: the quality of talking with too much pride
entries.definitionCN: 自夸习气；较 braggadocio 少一层「空」意
张扬做派；可指步态，braggadocio 侧重言辞
浮夸的大话（书面语）；源自加斯科尼人名声

entries.definition: loud, aggressive talk that means little
entries.definitionCN: 咆哮式空谈；侧重气势而非自夸

entries.definition: arrogant bragging, from Spanish don fanfarrón
entries.definitionCN: 夸夸其谈；源自西班牙语典故

normalIntro.en: Split it in two: BRAG plus a fake Italian tail makes a fake Italian bravo.
normalIntro.cn: 一分为二记：BRAG 加一条假意大利词尾，拼出一个假意大利剑客。

normal.en: the base is simply brag, to boast.

normal.cn: -adocio 模仿 Boccaccio 之类的意大利姓氏。

normal.en: Spenser coined it for a knight who boasts but never fights.
normal.cn: 斯宾塞为一名只吹不打的自夸骑士造了此名。

normal.en: it turned from a name into a common noun by the seventeenth century.
normal.cn: 十七世纪由人名转成普通名词。

abstract.en: An empty armor: loud outside, hollow inside.
abstract.cn: 一副空甲：外面震天响，里面空荡荡。

abstract.en: A peacock feather stuck on a borrowed helmet.
abstract.cn: 借来的盔盔上插一根孔雀羽。

abstract.en: The loudest voice in the room is often the emptiest.
abstract.cn: 屋里最响的声音往往最空。

examples.en: Critics called the manifesto mostly braggadocio, short on plans and long on promises.
examples.cn: 评论者称那份宣言大话居多，计划寥寥而许诺成山。

examples.en: Under all the braggadocio, the young boxer was terrified.
examples.cn: 大话底下的年轻拳手其实满心恐惧。

examples.en: Rap's tradition of braggadocio turns self-praise into an art form.
examples.cn: 说唱音乐的 braggadocio 传统把自夸变成了一门艺术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不赖格多丘」——「我不赖」说得格（个）多又久，堆成小山丘：说了「一丘」大话，就是 braggadocio。

root: 词基为中古英语 brag（吹嘘）+ 斯宾塞仿意大利语词尾 -adocio（戏仿意大利姓氏）；1590 年《仙后》中自夸骑士 Braggadocchio 之名转为普通名词。

sensesIntro.en: From the character's name, the word covers his talk, his manner, his like-minded persons, and even a whole group's swagger.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项由角色之名出发，涵盖其言谈、做派、同好之人，乃至整个群体的张扬气质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knight in borrowed armor boasting of fights he never fought
core.cn: 核心意象：身披借来盔甲的骑士，吹嘘自己从未打过的仗

branches.en: hollow noise: loud claims, empty middle
branches.cn: 空心的响声：口号震天，内里空空

branches.en: the style: swagger in speech and in prose
branches.cn: 风格：口头与笔头的浮夸做派

branches.en: the wearer: the person behind the mask
the stage moment: pre-fight talk that sells seats
branches.cn: 舞台时刻：卖票的赛前叫阵

branches.en: from one knight to a whole culture's swagger
branches.cn: 从一名骑士到一种文化的张扬

intro.en: A literary coinage: an English root wearing a borrowed Italian suit of endings.
intro.cn: 文学造词：英语词根套上一身借来的意大利式词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; the Italian flavor is decorative, not genetic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词；意大利风味是装饰性的，并非血统。

items.meaningCN: 斯宾塞笔下的自夸骑士

items.example: the coinage teases the Italian bravo
items.exampleCN: 造词戏仿意大利剑客 bravo
意大利语 occhio 意为眼睛

items.example: swagger is the walk, braggadocio the talk
